newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ANGELS HIRE COLLINS AS MANAGER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ANGELS HIRE COLLINS AS MANAGER.

text.p: Terry Collins, fired by the Houston Astros following a late-season collapse, was given a second chance when he was named manager of the California Angels on Monday.

Collins takes over an Angels team that finished in last place in the American League West with a 70-91 record. Marcel Lachemann resigned as Angels manager on August 6 and was replaced on an interim basis by John McNamara.

The 47-year-old Collins was fired as manager of the Astros last month and replaced by Larry Dierker. After climbing to 11 games over .500 (74-63) on August 31, Houston stumbled to a 8-17 record in September, including a nine-game losing streak.
The team finished at 82-80, six games behind the Central Division winning St Louis Cardinals.

Collins compiled a 224-197 (.532) record in three seasons at the helm in Houston, finishing second in the Central all three years. The 1995 squad ended up one game behind Colorado for a wild-card berth in the playoffs.
Collins managed in the minors from 1981-91, including eight years in the Dodgers organisation. He served as the Pittsburgh Pirates bullpen coach for two seasons prior to joining the Astros.
The Angels have had just one winning season since 1990, and that was in 1995, when they narrowly failed to make the playoffs by losing a one-game playoff to the Seattle Mariners.
